MARBIDA Better Regulations Office Anti-Red Tape Authority mvw.dilq.qov.ph OPINION NO. 79 s. 209=1 ATTN: Dear Dir. Marbida: LIZAMYL D. BUQUID Division Chief, Sectoral Division C This pertains to your request for an opinion on the Province of Sorsogon's Provincial Ordinance No. 23-2022 entitled: "AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING COMPREHENSIVE MECHANISM FOR THE EFFICIENT MANAGEMENT OF TRAFFIC FOR ALL VEHICLES TRAVERSING THE MAHARLIKA HIGHWAY TO THE PORT OF MATNOG BY ESTABLISHING A "BLUE LANE" AND A "ONE-STOP-SHOP", PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES". The request was premised by an issue raised by the representative/s of LGU-Matnog, Sorsogon, during your November 7, 2023 meeting with the Bureau of Local Government Supervision (BLGS). Per the Highlights of the Meeting furnished to us, the query is on the office/agency that should be responsible with the traffic management in Matnog, Sorsogon, and the legality of Provincial Ordinance 23-2002 or the Blue Lane Ordinance. It is likewise mentioned that the counsel for LGU-Matnog manifested non-amenability to the inclusion of the same in the proposed Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) on the Measures to Address the Congestion In and Around the Vicinity of Port of Matnog. On the issue of responsibility with traffic management, Sec. 16 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", is controlling: SECTION 16. General Welfare. - Every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied there from, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local government units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. At the outset, based on the above-cited provision, traffic management is the primary responsibility of the component Local Government Unit (LGU). We are of the opinion, "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

however, that the same does not discount the responsibility of the supervising LGU on matters that transcends matters cognizable by the component LGU. In the instant case, issues arising from the problem of Matnog port congestion affects not only the constituents of the Municipality of Matnog, Sorsogon. Being the gateway of Luzon to Visayas and Mindanao, all passengers and business entities transporting goods and merchandise from all regions within the country are affected. This is not a case where a supervising LGU cannot take responsibility. The problem persists and is evident, something that cannot be unseen by the local officials of the provincial LGU. We are reminded that the exercise of supervision by provincial LGUs over its component LGUs is constitutionally founded. Section 4, ArticleXof the 1987 Philippine Constitution provides: Section 4. The President of the Philippines shall exercise general supervision over local governments. Provinces with respect to component cities and municipalities, and cities and municipalities with respect to component barangays, shall ensure that the acts of their component units are within the scope of their prescribed powers and functions. Now that the provincial ordinance was enacted to address the Matnog Port Congestion, the Governor as the Local Chief Executive is dutybound to enforce the same. In view of its province-wide application, the Municipal Mayor of Matnog and all other Local Chief Executive of nearby municipalities that may be affected by port congestion and vehicle queuing are likewise duty-bound to abide by it and enforce it. We add that the efforts to mitigate the heavy traffic and long queueing brought about by the port congestion may be collaborated by other National Agencies having aligned functions and mandates. It is in view of the traffic congestion affecting the National Highway. On the issue of the legality of a provincial ordinance, the department is consistent with its stand that the same is a judicial matter. In the time being, what we can comment on is its enforceability anchored on the presumption of validity of legislative acts and enactments. Considering that enforceability is corollary to constitutionality, the resolution is deemed enforceable in the absence of any judicial declaration against its constitutionality. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to contrary opinion or ruling which may be rendered by competent authorities and the proper courts. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, Y AUT RITY THE SEC LLAMAS Unde retary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSE RULLLS-LRALLD/kbm DEBIE T. TORRES, CESO Director. Bugs MAYOR CATTLEYA M. SO W tnog.
